cohorts.subjects: Dry skeletons from the Hamann-Todd Osteological Collection, Cleveland, Ohio (held by the Cleveland Museum of Natural History, per the acknowledgments): treated and dried specimens of people who died in Cleveland between 1893 and 1938, with height and weight documented at death, sex and ethnic origin; 503 chosen at random; called American in the abstract and Table 5; 281 Caucasian and 222 African American. Excluded: congenital disease such as scoliosis (number not given); medical and surgical history largely unavailable. How levels were identified and whether any spine had a transitional segment is not stated.
cohorts.n_units: L1 to L5 of 503 skeletons, left and right pedicles measured and averaged (Inference: 2,515 vertebrae, 5,030 pedicles)
cohorts.ages: mean 47 yr, range 17 to 93 (text); Table 1 bands 15-24 to 85-94 yr; Table 3 bands <=30, 31-49, 50-69, >=70 yr

techniques.instrument: digital caliper reading to one hundredth of a millimetre (0.01 mm)
techniques.how: PH: caliper applied from the lateral side, in the sagittal plane, at the narrowest point of the pedicle along its long axis (cranial-caudal size). PW: caliper applied from below, in the transverse plane, at the narrowest point (medial-lateral size). Left and right pedicles measured and averaged; all vertebrae of one skeleton measured before the next. Left and right differed (P < 0.05) only for PH at L1 and L2.
techniques.magnification: not applicable, measured on the bone
techniques.observers: one examiner (C.C.Y.) measured every specimen; inter- and intrarater coefficients of variation 5.2% (1.5-16.8%) and 4.0% (1.7-6.2%) on 21 random samples, PH and PW not separated (Inference: a second, unnamed rater measured the 21 for the inter-rater figure)

within_paper: One cohort of its own: Tables 1 to 4, the CS column of Table 5, Figure 3 and the text values are all the same 503 Hamann-Todd skeletons, cut by age, sex, race, height and weight (Table 3's age, height and weight bands each sum to 503; Table 1's age bands differ from Table 3's), p. 1640 to 1645 (PDF 2 to 7). PH and PW were measured on the same vertebrae, p. 1640 (PDF 2). The reliability figures come from 21 random samples (Inference: drawn from the 503), p. 1640 (PDF 2). The comparison columns of Table 5 are other studies' subjects, not this paper's.
